title: Slow Cooker Sweet Potato & Black Bean Chili
description: Sweet potatoes, black beans, tomatoes, and mild spices cook into a hearty inexpensive meatless chili.

ingredients.item: medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced

substitutions: Use kidney or pinto beans for one can of black beans.
Use 3 cups peeled diced butternut squash instead of sweet potatoes.

steps.text: Add everything to the slow cooker.
Cook until the sweet potatoes are tender.

cookSteps.text: Add 2 diced sweet potatoes, 2 drained cans black beans, 1 can diced tomatoes, 1 can tomato sauce, 1 cup water or broth, 1 tablespoon chili powder, 1 teaspoon cumin, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon salt to the slow cooker. Stir well.
Cover and cook on HIGH for 4 hours, or until the sweet potatoes are completely tender.
Stir well, taste, and serve. Mash a few sweet potato pieces against the side if you want a thicker chili.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months.

title: Sheet-Pan Parmesan Cabbage & White Beans
description: Cabbage wedges and white beans roast together with garlic and Parmesan for a crisp-edged inexpensive dinner.

ingredients.item: green cabbage, cut into bite-size pieces

substitutions: Use chickpeas instead of white beans.
Use finely shredded cheddar during the final 5 minutes instead of Parmesan.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss 1/2 head chopped cabbage and 1 drained can white beans with 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper on a large sheet pan.
Spread into one layer and roast for 20 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the cabbage edges brown.
Sprinkle 1/2 cup Parmesan over the pan and roast 5 minutes more until the cheese is golden and the cabbage is tender.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat in a hot oven or skillet for the best texture.

title: Leftover Rice Pizza Bowls
description: Leftover rice gets a quick pizza-style makeover with tomato sauce, mozzarella, and whatever simple toppings are around.
equipment: microwave-safe bowls or small baking dish

ingredients.item: sliced mushrooms, peppers, olives, or other pizza topping

substitutions: Use cheddar or an Italian cheese blend instead of mozzarella.
Use leftover cooked pasta instead of rice.

cookSteps.text: Divide 2 cups cooked rice between 2 microwave-safe bowls. Stir 3/8 cup marinara into each bowl and sprinkle with 1/2 teaspoon Italian seasoning total.
Top each bowl with 1/2 cup shredded mozzarella and any optional pizza toppings.
Microwave each bowl until steaming hot and the cheese is melted, about 2–3 minutes. Let stand 1 minute before eating.

storage: Refrigerate assembled leftovers up to 3 days and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Small-Batch Chocolate Banana Muffins
description: One ripe banana makes six soft cocoa muffins, handy when you want a little baking without a dozen leftovers.
substitutions: Use white sugar instead of brown sugar.
Leave out the chocolate chips for a simpler cocoa-banana muffin.

steps.text: Mash and mix the wet ingredients.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease or line 6 muffin cups. Mash 1 ripe banana, then whisk in 1 egg, 1/4 cup brown sugar, and 2 tablespoons melted butter or oil.
Fold in 1/2 cup flour, 2 tablespoons cocoa powder, 1/2 teaspoon baking soda, and 1/8 teaspoon salt just until no dry flour remains. Fold in 2 tablespoons chocolate chips if using.
Divide the batter among 6 muffin cups and bake 16–18 minutes, until the tops spring back and a toothpick comes out without wet batter.

storage: Keep covered at room temperature up to 2 days or refrigerate up to 5 days. Freeze up to 2 months.
